claims.text: The starting material is an FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy multilayer with nanoscale layer thickness.
The as-deposited FCC/BCC interfaces are relatively coherent.
Controlled compositional tuning can reduce interface coherency.
Post-deposition annealing can reduce interface coherency.
Reduced interface coherency enhances atomic diffusion along FCC/BCC interfaces.
Enhanced interfacial diffusion promotes a transition from dislocation-mediated creep to interface-assisted creep.
The proposed creep-mechanism transition causes progressive plastic deformation under sustained loading.
Interface coherency is associated with atomic-scale distortions at the FCC/BCC interfaces.
Interface coherency is associated with local ordering at the FCC/BCC interfaces.
Increased lattice distortion enhances atomic diffusion pathways along the interfaces.
Incoherent interfaces enhance atomic diffusion pathways along the interfaces.
Under sustained stress, modified interfaces facilitate dislocation nucleation through diffusion-assisted processes.
Under sustained stress, modified interfaces facilitate dislocation motion through diffusion-assisted processes.
Multilayers with intentionally reduced interface coherency will have higher creep rates than coherent-interface baseline multilayers.
Multilayers with intentionally reduced interface coherency will show greater interface-localized diffusion than the baseline.
Multilayers with intentionally reduced interface coherency will show altered dislocation structures relative to the baseline.
A transition from dislocation-dominated to diffusion-assisted creep occurs after a critical interface-incoherency threshold is crossed.
Deformation in the coherent-interface baseline is primarily governed by dislocation glide.
Interface diffusion is limited in the coherent-interface baseline.
The proposed comparison requires fixed nanoscale layer thickness, comparable overall composition, creep-relevant temperature and stress, and preserved multilayer integrity.
